# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/server"
```

Package server is an OpenADR 3.1.0 VTN as an http.Handler.

The Server implements the REST API and its access rules. It leaves to the embedding program what a VTN deployment decides for itself: the listener and TLS, where tokens come from (auth.Validator) and where objects are kept (storage.Store).

Programs, events, reports, VENs and resources are always served. Subscriptions are served when the Server is given a way to deliver their notifications, a WebhookSender or WebSockets, and GET /notifiers when it has any way to notify, MQTT included. Without, they answer 501 Not Implemented, as the MQTT topic operations do without Config.MQTT.

Two things a Server can do are not part of OpenADR 3.1.0, and are off unless Config says otherwise: notifications over a WebSocket and resource groups. Both are extensions shared with OpenLEADR.

Mount the handler at the root of the API. To serve it under a path prefix, wrap it in http.StripPrefix.

## Types

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Store holds the VTN's objects. Required.
	Store storage.Store
	// Validator resolves bearer tokens. Required, except for a VTN that
	// only serves clients that do not authenticate (AllowAnonymous).
	Validator auth.Validator
	// TokenURL is the OAuth2 token endpoint that GET /auth/server announces
	// to clients. Required with a Validator, and an absolute http or https
	// URL: the schema says so, and clients of other implementations do not resolve a
	// relative reference. For a VTN that serves its own token endpoint (see
	// TokenHandler) it is the public URL of the API followed by /auth/token.
	TokenURL string
	// TokenHandler serves POST /auth/token, for a VTN that issues its own
	// tokens (see auth.Issuer). When nil the endpoint answers 501.
	TokenHandler http.Handler
	// Webhooks delivers notifications and verifies callback URLs; see
	// package notification/webhook for the implementation. When nil, the
	// VTN has no subscriptions to webhooks, and without WebSocket either,
	// no subscriptions at all.
	Webhooks WebhookSender
	// MQTT publishes notifications to a broker and makes the VTN announce
	// it; see package notification/mqtt for a publisher. When nil, the
	// MQTT topic operations answer 501.
	MQTT *MQTTConfig
	// WebSocket lets clients receive notifications over a WebSocket, which
	// is not part of OpenADR 3.1.0; see WebSocketConfig. When nil,
	// /notifiers/ws does not exist. Call Close when the VTN stops.
	WebSocket *WebSocketConfig
	// ResourceGroups makes the VTN serve /resource_groups, which is not
	// part of OpenADR 3.1.0: see openadr.ResourceGroup. Without it the
	// path does not exist.
	ResourceGroups bool
	// AllowAnonymous makes the VTN answer requests that carry no token, as
	// the specification allows for public information such as price
	// schedules ("Non-Authenticating VTNs"). Such a client can read the
	// programs and events that have no targets, and ask how the VTN
	// notifies; every other operation still needs a token. A request that
	// does carry a token is validated as usual.
	AllowAnonymous bool
	// DisableCompression turns off compression of responses. By default a
	// response of 1 KiB or more is compressed, with gzip or deflate, for a
	// client that accepts one of them.
	DisableCompression bool
	// Logger receives internal errors, with the method and the path of the
	// request and never its body or token; and at debug level one line
	// per request, with its operation, status and duration. Nil disables
	// logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Outbox makes webhook notifications survive: each is recorded there
	// before it is sent and forgotten when its webhook has confirmed it,
	// and what is still recorded is sent again, when the VTN starts and
	// while it runs. Delivery is then at least once across restarts, where
	// without an Outbox what is on its way when the VTN stops is lost.
	// storage.File is an Outbox as well as a Store; so is storage.Memory,
	// which lasts as long as the process and so only adds the sending
	// again. It needs Webhooks to be a ConfirmingSender, which
	// *webhook.Sender is, and Close to be called when the VTN stops.
	// Notifications by MQTT and over WebSockets are not kept.
	Outbox storage.Outbox
	// NotificationTTL is how long a notification that cannot be delivered
	// is kept before it is given up; a day when zero. Only with Outbox.
	NotificationTTL time.Duration
	// RedeliverEvery is how often the VTN hands to the sender again what
	// is recorded and not on its way; a minute when zero. Only with Outbox.
	RedeliverEvery time.Duration
	// Limiter decides, for every request of a client it has identified,
	// whether the VTN takes it now; see Limiter and NewRateLimiter. A
	// request it refuses is answered 429 with a Retry-After header, which
	// the clients of this module honour. Nil takes every request.
	Limiter Limiter
	// NotifyReads makes the VTN notify the subscribers that asked for the
	// operation READ whenever an object is read, by ID or in a search.
	// Off by default: OpenADR 3.1.0 lists READ among the operations of a
	// subscription and says nothing of what it means, it is one
	// notification per object per read, and it costs the VTN a look at
	// its subscriptions for every read. Without it a subscription to READ
	// is accepted and never notified of one.
	NotifyReads bool
	// Metrics receives a callback for every request, and, when it
	// implements them, for notifications and WebSockets; see Metrics. Nil
	// disables them.
	Metrics Metrics
	// MaxBodyBytes limits the size of a request body; 1 MiB when zero.
	MaxBodyBytes int64
	// Limits bounds what one client keeps in the VTN: by default at most
	// 100 subscriptions, each with at most 16 callback URLs. See Limits.
	Limits Limits
	// Now replaces the clock, for tests.
	Now func() time.Time
}
```

Config configures a Server.

### type ConfirmingSender

```go
type ConfirmingSender interface {
	WebhookSender
	// SendConfirmed is Send, and calls done exactly once: with nil when
	// the webhook confirmed the notification, and with an error when the
	// sender has given up on it. An error that has a method
	// Permanent() bool which returns true says that trying again is of no
	// use; any other, that it may be.
	SendConfirmed(callbackURL, bearerToken string, body []byte, done func(error))
}
```

ConfirmingSender is a WebhookSender that says what became of a notification, which is what it takes to keep notifications until they are delivered (Config.Outbox). \*webhook.Sender implements it.

### type Limiter

```go
type Limiter interface {
	// Allow reports whether the request is taken. clientID is the client
	// of the token, and empty for a client that did not authenticate, on a
	// VTN that allows that. op is the operation, as Metrics names it
	// ("GET /events/{id}"). When it returns false, retryAfter is how long
	// the client is told to wait; zero tells it nothing.
	Allow(clientID, op string) (ok bool, retryAfter time.Duration)
}
```

Limiter decides whether a VTN takes a request now. It is asked once for every request of a client the VTN has identified and found entitled to the operation: a request without a valid token, or without the scope, is refused before, and costs a Limiter nothing.

Implementations must be safe for concurrent use, and must not block: a request that has to wait is refused, with the time to wait.

### type Limits

```go
type Limits struct {
	// Subscriptions is the most subscriptions one client keeps; 100 when
	// zero.
	Subscriptions int
	// CallbackURLs is the most distinct callback URLs one subscription
	// names; 16 when zero. They are verified, when the subscription is
	// created or an update adds them, a few at a time.
	CallbackURLs int
	// VENs, Resources and Reports are the most of each that one client
	// keeps; no limit when zero. A VEN that reports for as long as it runs
	// makes ever more reports, so a limit on them needs the application to
	// delete old ones.
	VENs, Resources, Reports int
}
```

Limits bounds what one client keeps in the VTN. OpenADR 3.1.0 sets no such limits; a VTN that serves clients it does not fully trust needs them, because every write is checked against every subscription, and a subscription's callback URLs are each called to be verified.

A create that would pass a limit is answered 409 with a problem that says which: the client can delete some of what it keeps and try again. A negative limit is no limit.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnRequest is called when a request arrives.
	OnRequest(op string)
	// OnResponse is called when it has been answered, with the HTTP status
	// and how long that took. A request that opens a WebSocket is answered
	// when the WebSocket is open (status 101), not when it closes.
	OnResponse(op string, status int, duration time.Duration)
}
```

Metrics receives a callback for every request a VTN serves. The callbacks run on the goroutine of the request and must not block: count, observe, return. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

op names the operation by method and path as the specification writes it, such as "GET /events" or "PUT /programs/{id}". A request that is not an operation of the VTN (an unknown path, a method the path does not have) is "other". The set of values is small and fixed, so op is fit to be a label; the path of the request, with its IDs, would not be.

A value that also implements NotificationMetrics or SocketMetrics is told of those too.

Where a client can see an effect, the callback for it comes first: the opening of a WebSocket (OnResponse and OnSocketOpened) is reported before the handshake is answered, and a notification before it is handed to the sender, the broker or the WebSocket. A reading of the metrics taken after such an effect was observed includes it. An ordinary response is reported when the handler has written it, which its client may see a moment earlier.

### type RateLimiter

```go
type RateLimiter struct {
	// tokens per second

}
```

RateLimiter is a Limiter that gives each client a budget of requests: a token bucket per client ID. All clients that do not authenticate share one bucket.

#### func NewRateLimiter

```go
func NewRateLimiter(perSecond float64, burst int) *RateLimiter
```

NewRateLimiter returns a Limiter that lets each client make perSecond requests a second on average, and burst at once after a quiet time. A burst below 1 is 1.

It is a guard against a client that has gone wrong, a loop without a pause, not a defence against an attack: it counts requests of clients it knows, after their token was checked. What arrives without a valid token is for a gateway before the VTN to limit.

#### func (RateLimiter) Allow

```go
func (l *RateLimiter) Allow(clientID, _ string) (bool, time.Duration)
```

Allow implements Limiter.

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// The optional extensions of metrics, nil when it has not got them.

	// creating is held while a create that is limited by Limits counts

}
```

Server is a VTN. It is safe for concurrent use and holds no state besides its Store and, with Config.WebSocket, the connections of its clients.

#### func New

```go
func New(cfg Config) (*Server, error)
```

New returns a Server for cfg.

#### func (Server) Close

```go
func (s *Server) Close() error
```

Close ends what the Server has running of its own: the WebSockets of its clients, which the HTTP server that serves it does not close when it shuts down, because those connections are no longer its own, and the sending again of recorded notifications (Config.Outbox). New WebSockets are refused after. A Server with neither has nothing to close.

ServeHTTP implements http.Handler.

### type WebSocketConfig

```go
type WebSocketConfig struct {
	// PingInterval is how often the VTN pings a connected client; a client
	// that does not answer two pings is disconnected. 30 seconds when zero.
	PingInterval time.Duration
	// MaxPerClient is the number of connections one client may have open;
	// one more is refused with 409. 4 when zero.
	MaxPerClient int
	// Queue is the number of notifications that may wait for one
	// connection. A connection whose queue is full is closed. 256 when zero.
	Queue int
}
```

WebSocketConfig is the WebSocket binding of a VTN's notifications, which is not part of OpenADR 3.1.0: an extension of OpenLEADR that this module shares. A client opens GET /notifiers/ws with its bearer token and is sent, as text messages, the notifications of its subscriptions that name the mechanism WEBSOCKET. The zero value is a usable configuration.

A WebSocket is not a queue. What happens while a client is not connected it is not told, and a client that reads too slowly is disconnected; a client catches up by searching, as it does after any reconnect.

### type WebhookSender

```go
type WebhookSender interface {
	// Verify checks, before a subscription is accepted, that a callback
	// URL may be used and that a webhook answers there. Its error is shown
	// to the client that named the URL.
	Verify(ctx context.Context, callbackURL string) error
	// Send delivers a notification in the background and returns at once.
	// bearerToken is empty when the subscription has none.
	Send(callbackURL, bearerToken string, body []byte)
}
```

WebhookSender is what the VTN needs to notify by webhook. \*webhook.Sender implements it.
